label: Fish Audio Drama 3 on Comfy (voice clone; paid)

capabilities._note: Fish Audio's Drama 3 hosted, through ComfyUI's partner nodes (Fish Audio Text to Speech, model drama-3; Fish Audio Instant Voice Clone): paid per take, billed to the Comfy API key in Settings (backends.partner sends it with the job), nothing to download. Comfy's docs gave about $14.30 per million bytes of text at the launch offer, $35.75 from 2026-11-13. Sent the words alone. A voice sample is cloned: the sample cut between words to 10-30 s (Fish's own advice for a clone) and sent through Instant Voice Clone, which makes a private voice on Fish Audio's side for that take; with none, Fish picks a voice, steered by the series config's `voice` line as a bracketed direction (target.py). The node's seed only says when to run again (target.py sets it from the take's): Fish's results aren't repeatable, so a take isn't made the same twice. Not run here: nothing paid was.

template._note: The model decides the length (it ends at end of speech): these only bound what a sample is asked to say.

recipe._note: The words alone (targets/audio/common.py words_line / words_prompt); the `voice` line only as a direction, and only with no sample.

binding._note: The partner node at its defaults for drama-3 (temperature 0.7, top_p 0.7, speed 1, volume 0, normalize on), its inputs as ComfyUI's API takes a dynamic combo's (`model` the option, `model.<input>` its own), and SaveAudio. With a sample, target.py adds LoadAudio and Instant Voice Clone into `model.voices.voice0`. Both partner nodes are marked `_meta.partner`: the take is counted against Settings' paid limit (runner.reserve). H3SaveRefAudio takes SaveAudio's place.

nodes._note: Beyond the workflow's own classes: what a clone adds (target.py), all ComfyUI's own.
